# NOTES ON TWO BOOKS (compact reference; use instead of the original text)

## BOOK 1: "Frank Merriwell's Support; Or, A Triple Play" by Burt L. Standish (Street & Smith, 1901; Gutenberg #62719)

### Setting and cast
- Team: Frank Merriwell's Yale nine, touring the West/East. Members: Frank Merriwell (pitcher, sprained wrist; double-shoot pitch; later reverse curve), Dick Merriwell (younger half-brother, ~14, learns pitching; jump ball), Bart Hodge (catcher, dark-faced), Jack Ready (3rd base, jokester, speaks in florid jargon), Harry Rattleton (2nd base, mixes words, "dim-jandy"), Greg Carker (socialist-talking, pessimist), Bruce Browning (1st base, big, lazy), Berlin Carson (rf/ss), Joe Gamp (cf, long-legged New Hampshire youth, stutters), John Swiftwing (lf, Indian, ex-Carlisle).
- Old Joe Crowfoot: old Indian, Dick's guardian/mentor, wrapped in dirty red blanket, black pipe; speaks broken English ("Heap big," "Injun Heart," "Steady Hand" = Frank). Previously shot; once tried to kill Frank; now reconciled.
- Juan Delores: Spanish refugee who raised Dick. Felicia: Dick's love (Felicia, "Little Star Eyes"); her father Mr. Delores.
- Merriwell's father willed Frank guardianship of Dick.
- Fardale: school where Dick will go.

### Book 1 events in order
1. **Ch. I (Omaha Stars game):** 7th inning; Merriwell's team scoreless; Omaha Stars lead 2–0 (runs in 1st and 5th). Frank's wrist twists on first pitch of 7th; he delays; umpire Derring calls two balls. Hanson (Stars' heavy hitter) hits line drive; Swiftwing, Gamp chase; Gamp throws to plate; Bart tags Hanson at plate ("Out!") after bore him into ground. Frank pitches out of jam with reverse curve; Dorrity (Stars captain, 1st base) strikes out; Batch (pitcher) popped up; Rattleton caught between bases; Carker's single; Ready's hit. Frank scores from 3rd on Carker hit (slide). Bart's single lets Merry's team lead.
2. **Ch. II:** Ready scores; Hazen (red-faced gambler, stout, stubby mustache) and Wescott (slender, blue suit) in stands; Hazen bet ~$1,000 on Stars, Wescott $200. Hazen offers Frank $50, then $100, then $200 to throw the game; Frank flings money back; Hazen claims agreement; Frank shakes him; officer removes Hazen. Hazen signals umpire Derring to make bad calls; Derring calls strikes on Gamp; Gamp's stutter-jibes; Stars' hitting. Merriwell's team given strikes; Derring's bad calls; Stars tie 2–2 (O'Grady double).
3. **Ch. III:** Derring miscalls Swiftwing's catch ("picked up"); mob forms; Frank protects Derring from mob; Dorrity asks for Chop Morrisy as new umpire; Derring declares forfeit 9–0; Dorrity refuses; Derring removed.
4. **Ch. IV:** Frank refuses to play unless calls fixed; Dorrity reluctant. Ninth inning: Maloney's Teller dropped-ball call; Stars win 3–2 when Corrigan scores on Bruce's wild throw. Merriwell defeated; defeat blamed on ragged support.
5. **Ch. V:** In Frank's room at hotel: team mourns; Old Joe considered mascot; Dick expected by letter. Frank challenges Manager Wilson (Stars) to return game, winner-take-gate; Wilson accepts. Dick's letter says he arrives next morning with Crowfoot. Derring confronts Frank drunk; threatens to shoot; Frank punches Derring; Hazen draws revolver; Frank kicks it away, returns it empty; takes Derring's gun.
6. **Ch. VI:** Dick and Old Joe arrive in Omaha. Frank asks Crowfoot to stay with Dick; Crowfoot agrees ("Injun Heart"; "you shall be his father"). Hazen and Derring mock; Dick's bet of $1,000 with Hazen; Frank forbids gambling; Hazen insists Dick is squealer; Frank gives Dick permission to bet only if winnings go to charity; Hazen to meet Dick at hotel office.
7. **Ch. VII:** Game 2 with Stars; Dick plays short; Frank pitches? No—Dick pitches, Frank plays short/Dick as pitcher. Dick strikes out Teller with hot ball; great fielding. Score tied 1–1 after 4th. Dick pitches with jump ball, drop, speed; Dick's bunt-hit; stolen bases; Old Joe's yell; Dick delivers winning run in 9th; Stars lose 2–1 (Dick stole home with winning run, actually Dick scored on Bart's grounder past second). Hazen loses bets.
8. **Ch. VIII (One to Nothing title, actually chapter VIII–IX):** Dick's catches; Stars score.
9. **Ch. X–XII (Minneapolis/St. Paul):** Foley hurt by Prince's spike; St. Paul's Trueman takes "jay" pitcher—actually Frank disguised as countryman with carrot hair, derby, Mud Creek pitching; uses double-shoot; Old Joe and stutter-friend Joe on bleachers; Frank hits home run, tie; Minneapolis bribes; poison in vichy: Dowling bribes waiter Pete. Frank wins with "jay" disguise.
10. **Ch. XIII–XV:** Old Joe war-whoop; Frank unmasked by hotel crowd; "Yale cheer." Minneapolis challenge; Bates, Dowling; Dowling offers $200 to throw game; Frank punches Dowling; Yale friends (Breka Co ax song).
11. **Ch. XVI–XIX (Minneapolis challenge game):** Dowling drugged Frank's vichy (via waiter Pete); Frank dizzy; Dick pitches with both hands (jump ball); Frank hits home run over fence to win 2–1 in 9th; Dick thrashes bully Squinty Jim McCann (Dick's first fight at Philadelphia, Old Joe defends with knife); Robinson (Phila. Athletics manager) challenges Frank.
12. **Ch. XX–XXV (Athletics game, Philadelphia):** Bud McCann (catcher, pugilist, brother of Squinty) throws bat tripping Frank; McCann beaten by Frank; McCann spikes Dick, Frank knocks out McCann; Robinson plays; Dick bunt-hits; Dick triple-play (catch of Maloney line drive, tagged Robinson); Frank 5–4 win on Dick's triple play.
13. **Ch. XXVI–XXIX (New York, Mysteries):** Jack Hazard challenge; the Mysteries = Frank's Yale friends (Gene Skelding, Starbright, Mason, Oliver Packard, Dismal Jones, Hans Dunnerwurst, Ephraim Gallup, Barney Mulloy, Dade Morgan pitcher). Dick homesick (Felicia). Inza Burrage and Elsie Bellwood in stands with Yale banners. Frank sends Dick to pitch. Dick starts poorly then recovers.
14. **Ch. XXX–XXXIII (NY finale):** Dick wins game; Old Joe kills rabid dog (Nero, owned by man with dog) with knife thrown at it after Dick hits dog's mouth with ball; Dick scores winning run stealing home; Inza gives Dick Yale blue badge.

Book 1 ends: "THE END." Note: next title No. 212 "Dick Merriwell at the Olympics."

## BOOK 2: "Dick Merriwell's Heroic Players; Or, How the Yale Nine Won the Championship" by Burt L. Standish (Street & Smith, 1912; Gutenberg #63608)

### Setting and cast
- Yale nine: Jim Phillips (sophomore pitcher, captain-elect), Bill Brady (big sophomore catcher, father owns Elm National Bank stock), Harry Maxwell (outfielder), Sam Taylor (senior catcher), Bob Gray (senior pitcher), Tom Sherman (senior 1st base, captain), Jackson (2nd base, junior), Steve Carter (3rd base), Jack Tempest (Virginian sprinter), Woeful Watson (pessimist sophomore), Gurney (sophomore), Winston (substitute pitcher), Horton (ss), Green, Brayson, Tuthill (country club men), Caxton (cf), Dick Merriwell (universal coach; now out of college; going to Olympics/Sweden; Maine lumber business with Chester Arlington, sister June).
- Harvard: Bowen (catcher, captain), Briggs (star pitcher), Wooley, Reid (shortstop), Farquar, Renshaw, Hazlitt, Hobson (ex-Harvard pitcher). Neilson = Harvard crew coach; Thompson (younger Harvard coach).
- Yale antagonists: Parker (junior, football guard, drinks; hates Merriwell); Carpenter (grind, glasses; Shesgren's friend); Shesgren (sophomore, glasses, small, blue eyes, thin voice; repents); Paul Foote (undersized, smokes; father rowed on crew; wants "Y"); Gurney.
- Crew: Murchison (stroke, captain), Flagg (#7), Rogers (cox), Harper (bow). Assistant coaches Benton and Hargreaves.
- Villains: Chetwind (real-estate broker, country club member); Harding (gambler, father boss of New Haven); Barrows (gambler, "socialist" con man); Svenson (Scandinavian skipper of schooner *Marina*, Gloucester), Dennison (weak investor), Bascom (wireless man, electromagnet expert), Barnes (Harding's agent), Marsten (gambler, "Johnny", house with bell-mirror system), Riggs (paying teller, Elm National, stole $1,000), Phelps (lumber financier), Bromlow (bank president), Hastings (cashier), Detective Jones (New Haven police).

### Book 2 events in order
1. **Ch I:** Jim studying math; Bill Brady scouts Harvard (Briggs shut out Amherst). Practice at field; Dick coaches.
2. **Ch II:** Gurney bets; Watson pessimism; Carpenter and Shesgren jealous; Parker insults Tempest; Parker recruits sophomores against Phillips.
3. **Ch III:** Country club asks Phillips to pitch vs Boston Athletic Association (Hobson's team); Dick permits; Parker tells sophomores to befriend Phillips.
4. **Ch IV:** Game at New Haven: Jim vs Hobson; Phillips wins 1-run game. Bowen praises. Carpenter visits Jim; Jim receives registered letter (second letter vanishes).
5. **Ch V:** Harvard protest (Bowen): Phillips paid $100 registered letter by Chetwind. Dick investigates; Chetwind refuses name. Dick finds Carpenter visited.
6. **Ch VI–VII:** Receipt signed by Jim; Carter reveals Parker's blurting.
7. **Ch VIII:** Parker's plot: Shesgren tied; Carpenter hides letter; Parker removes money; marked bills.
8. **Ch IX:** Letter found by Jim under carpet; empty envelope with blank sheet; Chetwind identifies Shesgren as agent.
9. **Ch X:** Shesgren confesses; Dick slits envelopes with Parker's knife (nick evidence); Parker confesses; withdraws candidacy.
10. **Ch XI:** Dick arranges Harvard withdrawal; Jim kidnapped in Boston cab; flees; Brady searches.
11. **Ch XII:** Jim escapes by stealing aircraft (biplane); arrives at Harvard game; Yale wins game 1 by 1–0 (Carter steals; Jim's wild pitch with cap trick).
12. **Ch XIII–XIV:** Parker's withdrawal; Foote recruits; conspiracy vs Gray & Taylor; Parker confronts Dick; Parker steals confession; Jack Tempest sees.
13. **Ch XV–XVI:** Parker swaps confession paper; Taylor and Gray cribbing charge (blank history exam pages); Dick finds notes; Foote plants evidence.
14. **Ch XVII–XVIII:** Dean; Gray and Taylor suspended; Canfield; Harvard wins game 2 (Winston pitching); series tied.
15. **Ch XIX:** Finger prints found; Foote's plot; Gray cleared.
16. **Ch XX–XXIII:** Foote & Parker; Jim locked in freight car by Foote (ventriloquist baby cry); Brady finds Parker; Foote caught via bread finger prints (Detective Jones); Jim rescued at Kingston NY car 34,576 Big Four; Jim pitches game 3 Yale wins championship on triple play (left-hand catch). Jim elected captain.
17. **Ch XXIV–XXVIII:** Crew trouble: freshmen beat varsity; magnetic keels (iron groove); Harding scheme; Barrows and Svenson's *Marina* plot to make crew slow via electromagnet coil in motor boats; wireless messages.
18. **Ch XXIX–XXXIV:** Harding confronted, released; Brady & Phillips on *Marina*; Jim swims; sabotage of *Marina* (Jim scuttles it); Jim discovers model shell; boat race: Yale wins varsity by under 2 seconds; four-oar and freshman crews also won; Barrows's model torpedo stopped by Jim.
19. **Ch XXXV:** Boston challenges again (July 4 game); Dick plans team.
20. **Ch XXXVI–XLII:** Foote gambles at Marsten's; Barrows recruits Foote; Riggs in debt; bank robbery plot (fake $100 notes, Dick's $5,000 deposit); Jim catches robbers, knocked out; Riggs flees; counterfeit deposit framed on Dick and Jim; watchman found.
21. **Ch XLIII–XLV:** Barrows arrested in NY, 5 years; Riggs suspended sentence; Jim cleared. July 4: Yale beats Boston 8–7; Jim pitches through; Dick captains; triple bunt plays; Jim's final bunt-out at first on technicality.

Book 2 ends "THE END." Next title: No. 212 "Dick Merriwell at the Olympics" (noted in Book 2 back matter; back matter also lists Frank Merriwell Jr. and Alger/Stratemeyer/Optic/Nick Carter/Diamond Dick/Jack Harkaway series lists, not story content).
